turns.prompt:
You are given one attached CSV file:
  - nlo_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE crystalline materials whose properties are
    NOT given, columns `candidate_id`, `formula` and `poscar` (the crystal
    structure, in POSCAR format).

No property values are provided. Using your knowledge of crystal optics,
crystal symmetry and structure-property relationships, select the 5
candidates with the LARGEST SHG tensor component |d_ij| (pm/V) that also
satisfy a transparency requirement: the band gap must be at least 3 eV. Band
gaps are NOT given for the pool -- you must infer them. A selected candidate
whose band gap is below the threshold scores zero.

Reason from the structures, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
The SHG tensor vanishes in centrosymmetric crystals, so only non-centrosymmetric candidates can be competitive. All of the adamantine (tetrahedrally bonded, valence-electron count 4) chalcogenides in the pool satisfy this requirement; they are wurtzite- or zincblende-derived superstructures whose polar space groups permit a sizable \(d_{ij}\).

Among those compounds the magnitude of \(d_{ij}\) is controlled by the usual structure–property trends of crystal optics: larger linear susceptibility (higher density, heavier/more polarizable atoms) and a smaller gap both increase \(d\). Miller’s rule then implies that the Li–Zn–Ga–Se family (formally \(2\,\mathrm{LiGaSe}_2+\mathrm{ZnSe}\)) must lie at the top of the list. Their composition-weighted gap is \(\approx 3.03\,\mathrm{eV}\) (LiGaSe\(_2\) 3.13 eV, ZnSe 2.82 eV), satisfying the transparency constraint, while the presence of Zn and Se yields a higher refractive index than the Mg or S analogues.

Cell volumes of the six Li\(_2\)ZnGa\(_2\)Se\(_5\) polymorphs range from 236 to 275 Å\(^3\). The five densest members therefore possess the largest oscillator strength per volume and the largest \(|d_{ij}|\):

Final: c009, c012, c010, c013, c011
